notes: Lead profile: mid-stage ecommerce SaaS (B2B merchants). Using a hosted storefront + support chat. Small engineering team, prefers self-serve with clear guardrails.
Primary ask: hosted API that can survive marketing/feature rollouts without user-visible 429s. Wants guidance on quotas, concurrency, and backoff behavior.

Observed behavior in sandbox: during an aggressive ramp (1k-1.2k rps sustained for 2m) they saw ~6% 429s concentrated in a single API key. Quote from CTO: 'Can't have 429s during launches — churn risk is real.'

Technical constraints: token-cost sensitive, expect bursty daily spikes tied to push notifications and email campaigns. Typical baseline traffic ~30 rps; spikes up to ~1k rps for 30-90s windows during campaigns.
Desired SLOs and POC metrics: p95 generation latency <200ms (edge-region customers), 429s <1% during defined burst profile, predictable per-month cost within +/-15%.

Rate-limit wishlist (customer): per-api-key concurrency soft-limit 20, sustained per-key QPS 10, account-level token bucket with burst allowance to 2.5x for 60s, clear headers for X-RateLimit-*, and a webhook/alert on sustained throttling.

Suggested Redwood features to highlight: burst capacity, graceful 429s with Retry-After, per-key quotas, usage analytics, automatic prefix caching for common prompts, and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization to lower unit cost.

POC plan: 2-week sandbox; Redwood to provide traffic-shaping config + backoff sample; BerylBay to run 3 staged ramps (100 rps, 500 rps, 1.2k rps) and share request logs/429 incidence. Acceptance: <1% 429s at target burst, <10% cost delta vs baseline estimate.
Commercials: SMB pricing with burst buffer option preferred. Asked whether there is an overage bucket vs immediate hard quota. AE to follow up with pricing deck link (sent).
